title: Repository structure: application, environment and configuration

videos.script: A repository that works for one environment starts to hurt at the second. {{hurt}} Three things vary in what you describe. The application, the environment, and the configuration that joins them. They change at different speeds, by different people. A good layout gives each one its own place. {{axes}} So the application's source moves to a repository of its own, and the two meet at one point, the image. {{repos}} Environments become directories on one branch, not branches. You will see why merging one branch into another is the wrong way to promote. {{dirs}} Then production arrives, and you promote a real release. Version 1.1 is built once, runs in staging, and reaches production through a pull request one line long. {{promote}} Last, who owns which directory, and how the same layout grows to many clusters. {{owners}}
